source.title: Notes on open questions within density functional theory (existence of a derivative of the Lieb functional in a restricted sense and non-interacting v-representability)

accepted.question_text: For the interacting Lieb functional FL[n] in density functional theory, can one prove that FL[n] admits a derivative in a restricted or weak sense for every interacting ensemble v-representable density n in the set B, even though FL[n] is nowhere Gateaux differentiable on the full Banach space X? Any such result must identify physically meaningful perturbation directions that preserve particle number and keep perturbed densities inside the admissible density set S, while still making the directional derivative finite and linear on that restricted class.
accepted.context_brief: Restricted differentiability of the interacting Lieb functional

evidence.quote: The existence of a derivative of the Lieb functional in the general case thus still represents an open question.
Nevertheless, would FL[n] admit some weaker notion of a derivative in the subset B ⊂ S ? This would be sufficient for most of previous KS scheme considerations to hold.
A more general demonstration that at least relaxes all constraints on B would be necessary for most of previous KS scheme considerations to hold. This still represents an open question.

accepted.question_text: Is the non-interacting v-representability conjecture true, meaning that every interacting ensemble v-representable ground-state density in the set B can be reproduced exactly by some non-interacting Kohn-Sham system, so that B equals the set Bs of non-interacting ensemble v-representable densities? Equivalently, when a sequence of non-interacting densities nε in Bs converges to an interacting density n in B, does the limit always correspond to an actually attainable non-interacting density rather than merely an arbitrarily good approximation?
accepted.context_brief: Exact non-interacting representability of interacting densities

evidence.quote: Now, even if the Lieb functional could be proven admit a derivative in a restricted sense, a further difficulty may occur: the interacting and non-interacting Lieb functionals may not be differentiable on the same set. This difficulty has been called "non-interacting v-representability question"

There is (even conjecturing that a KS potential can rigorously be defined from the Lieb functional) no proof that the sets B and Bs are equal. Considering B = Bs, important for the complete foundation of the Lieb functional-based KS scheme, thus represents a further conjecture called "non-interacting v-representability conjecture".

accepted.question_text: Does the Kohn-Sham potential functional vs[ns], defined for non-interacting ensemble v-representable densities ns in Bs, admit a derivative in a restricted sense for every ns in Bs, and is that derivative bounded? The notes identify a positive answer as sufficient to prove the non-interacting v-representability conjecture, but they also note that establishing such a derivative rigorously is difficult, especially in degenerate cases, and that the inverse response kernel χs^-1[vs[ns]] is unbounded.
accepted.context_brief: Restricted bounded derivative of the Kohn-Sham potential

evidence.quote: Theorem 4.2 (Non-interacting v-representability and derivative of the KS potential). If a derivative of vs[ns] exists in a restricted sense for ns ∈ Bs and if this derivative is bounded, then the non-interacting v-representability conjecture is true.
In the following, we give some static linear response-based elements that hopefully contribute to the reflection on the existence of some derivative of vs[ns].

However, as αj can become arbitrailly close to 0, 1/αj is not bounded. This implies that the representation of −χ−1 s [vs[ns]] in the orthonormal eigenvector basis is not bounded, so as its representations in any other basis. So, even if it was possible to rigorously demonstrate that χ−1 s [vs[ns]] represents a derivative of the KS potential in a restricted sense, the unboundedness of χ−1 s [vs[ns]] would not allow to conclude that the non-interacting v-representability conjecture is true
